boards.title: Your First Weekend at The College of Saint Scholastica, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure first-weekend sequence that starts on campus and expands into Duluth’s public waterfront, parks, and trails.

cards.title: Start by finding the Student Center
cards.subtitle: Campus hub · Friday afternoon
cards.notes: Use the common areas to get oriented, then check the Student Activities lounge for ways to connect with a club or campus program.
cards.short_summary: Begin with a clear campus meeting point and a look at student-life resources.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Center has 10 common areas, an outdoor patio, Student Activities offices and lounge, Campus Ministry offices, study rooms, and study booths.
cards.access_notes: A campus facility; confirm building access and any weekend programming with the College.

cards.entity_name: The College of St. Scholastica Library
cards.title: Make a quiet library stop
cards.subtitle: Three floors of study space · Friday afternoon
cards.notes: Walk through the library’s quiet and group-study areas so you know where to return when coursework begins; ask staff about available services.
cards.short_summary: A calm on-campus stop that establishes a practical study base.
cards.evidence_claim: The College library has three floors with designated quiet and group-study areas and welcomes visitors and local users.
cards.source_title: Library Resources | The College of St. Scholastica
cards.access_notes: Visitor and borrower access have separate conditions; check with the library’s main desk for current details.

cards.title: Move around at Burns Wellness Commons
cards.subtitle: Campus recreation · Friday afternoon
cards.notes: If you are eligible to use the facility, choose a simple first visit: walk the track, use open recreation, or ask the info desk about reservations.
cards.short_summary: Sample a campus recreation facility before planning a longer workout.
cards.evidence_claim: Burns Wellness Commons includes indoor running tracks, multipurpose courts, a weight room, cardio mezzanine, climbing wall, Reif Gymnasium, and locker rooms.
cards.access_notes: Facilities are available to current students, faculty, and staff; the College lists regular hours as Monday–Friday, 7 a.m.–7 p.m., with weekend closure.

cards.title: Check the Saints schedule at Reif Gymnasium
cards.subtitle: Campus athletics · Friday evening
cards.notes: Look for a scheduled basketball or volleyball game and attend only if an event is listed; it is an easy way to see a campus venue in use.
cards.short_summary: A conditional event stop anchored to the College’s indoor athletics venue.
cards.evidence_claim: Reif Gymnasium contains the main basketball and volleyball courts, plus two side basketball or volleyball courts.
cards.access_notes: Attend when a College athletics or recreation event is scheduled; verify event access and admission before going.

cards.title: Plan an Outdoor Pursuit outing
cards.subtitle: Beginner-friendly campus activity · Saturday morning
cards.notes: Ask Outdoor Pursuit about a current beginner-friendly trip or use the office to plan a later outing with appropriate gear and conditions.
cards.short_summary: Turn an interest in Duluth’s outdoors into a structured, supported next step.
cards.evidence_claim: Outdoor Pursuit provides guided activities to the College community, describes its adventures as beginner-friendly, and offers adaptive options.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Recreation at St. Scholastica: Explore Campus Life
cards.access_notes: Programming and rental availability vary; contact Outdoor Pursuit before relying on a particular trip or gear item.

cards.title: Take in Enger Park’s grounds
cards.subtitle: 1601 Enger Tower Drive · Saturday midday
cards.notes: Follow a marked trail or pause near the Peace Bell and gardens; use the park features listed by the city and check seasonal tower access first.
cards.short_summary: A city park stop with trails, gardens, and a landmark tower.
cards.evidence_claim: Enger Park includes hiking trails, picnic facilities, a public-access restroom, the American-Japanese Peace Bell, and Enger Tower.
cards.source_title: Enger Park | City of Duluth, MN
cards.access_notes: The city says the park entry gate and tower doors close when snow arrives and reopen annually on May 1, weather permitting.

cards.title: Walk through Canal Park
cards.subtitle: Duluth Ship Canal · Saturday afternoon
cards.notes: Use the waterfront public space as a short orientation walk, keeping to designated paths and taking time to identify the canal and Aerial Bridge.
cards.short_summary: A waterfront district stop centered on Duluth’s ship canal.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies Canal Park as land on either side of the federally owned canal and notes the Aerial Bridge and Lake Superior Maritime Visitor Center there.
cards.source_title: Canal Park | City of Duluth, MN
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor public area; observe posted rules, weather conditions, and any construction or event restrictions.

cards.title: Continue along the Lakewalk
cards.subtitle: Waterfront trail · Saturday afternoon
cards.notes: Choose a comfortable out-and-back segment, share the path with other users, and turn around early if weather, footing, or daylight is unsuitable.
cards.short_summary: Extend the waterfront visit with a flexible pedestrian-and-bicycle trail walk.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists the Lakewalk among its paved and gravel trails open to pedestrians and bicyclists.
cards.source_title: Paved Trails | City of Duluth, MN
cards.access_notes: Trail conditions can change; use the city’s parks and trails information and follow posted guidance.

cards.title: Pause at Leif Erikson Park
cards.subtitle: 11th Ave E & London Road · Saturday afternoon
cards.notes: Walk through the park beside Lake Superior and look for the Rose Garden, historic amphitheater, and the Lakewalk route through the grounds.
cards.short_summary: A named lakeside park that links garden, trail, and amphitheater features.
cards.evidence_claim: Leif Erikson Park includes the Duluth Rose Garden, a historic amphitheater stage, and the Lakewalk; the city lists paved trail and beach access among its features.
cards.source_title: Leif Erikson Park | City of Duluth, MN
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor city park; use designated paths and observe posted park rules or event-related restrictions.

cards.title: Finish with a Hartley Park trail walk
cards.subtitle: 3001 Woodland Avenue · Sunday daytime
cards.notes: Pick a short multi-purpose trail, bring appropriate footwear, and leave enough time to return before conditions change; share the trail courteously.
cards.short_summary: Close the weekend with a nearby wooded trail network and nature-center setting.
cards.evidence_claim: Hartley Park is a 640-acre park with ten miles of multi-purpose trails through forest and wetlands and is home to Hartley Nature Center.
cards.source_title: Hartley Park | City of Duluth, MN
cards.access_notes: The city lists hiking, biking, mountain-bike, cross-country-ski, birding, and public-restroom features; select a route suited to current conditions.
